name: Left Upper Lobe
description: Two-lobed lung (upper, lower) separated by the oblique fissure. Smaller than the right due to the cardiac notch accommodating the heart. The lingula is the tongue-like projection of the left upper lobe, analogous to the right middle lobe. On CT: assess parenchyma, fissure, airways, and vasculature.

name: Left Lower Lobe
description: Two-lobed lung (upper, lower) separated by the oblique fissure. Smaller than the right due to the cardiac notch accommodating the heart. The lingula is the tongue-like projection of the left upper lobe, analogous to the right middle lobe. On CT: assess parenchyma, fissure, airways, and vasculature.

name: Right Upper Lobe
description: Three-lobed lung (upper, middle, lower) separated by the oblique and horizontal fissures. Slightly larger than the left lung. The right main bronchus is wider, shorter, and more vertical — aspirated foreign bodies preferentially enter the right side. On CT: assess parenchyma, fissures, airways, and vasculature.

name: Right Lower Lobe
description: Three-lobed lung (upper, middle, lower) separated by the oblique and horizontal fissures. Slightly larger than the left lung. The right main bronchus is wider, shorter, and more vertical — aspirated foreign bodies preferentially enter the right side. On CT: assess parenchyma, fissures, airways, and vasculature.

name: Esophagus
description: Muscular tube extending from the pharynx (C6) to the gastroesophageal junction (T11). Posterior to the trachea in the upper mediastinum, then courses left of midline in the posterior mediastinum. On CT: assess wall thickness (<3 mm normal when distended), masses, varices, and hiatal herniation.

name: Trachea
description: Cartilaginous airway extending from the cricoid cartilage (C6) to the carina (T4–T5) where it bifurcates into right and left main bronchi. C-shaped cartilage rings anterolaterally with a membranous posterior wall. On CT: assess caliber, wall thickening, tracheomalacia, and extrinsic compression.

name: T7 Vertebra
description: Twelve thoracic vertebrae (T1–T12) forming the posterior thoracic wall. Each articulates with a pair of ribs via costovertebral joints. On CT: assess vertebral body height and density (compression fractures, metastases), pedicles, spinal canal diameter, and disc spaces.

name: T6 Vertebra
description: Twelve thoracic vertebrae (T1–T12) forming the posterior thoracic wall. Each articulates with a pair of ribs via costovertebral joints. On CT: assess vertebral body height and density (compression fractures, metastases), pedicles, spinal canal diameter, and disc spaces.

name: T5 Vertebra
description: Twelve thoracic vertebrae (T1–T12) forming the posterior thoracic wall. Each articulates with a pair of ribs via costovertebral joints. On CT: assess vertebral body height and density (compression fractures, metastases), pedicles, spinal canal diameter, and disc spaces.

name: Aorta
description: Largest artery in the body. Ascending aorta arises from the aortic valve, arches over the left main bronchus, then descends through the thorax. On CT: assess diameter at standard levels (sinuses, mid-ascending, arch, isthmus, descending), wall calcification, intramural hematoma, dissection flap, and ulceration.

name: Superior Vena Cava
description: Large vein formed by confluence of the right and left brachiocephalic veins, draining the head, neck, upper limbs, and thorax into the right atrium. On CT: assess for thrombosis (SVC syndrome), compression by mediastinal masses, and catheter tip position.

name: Spinal Cord
description: Twelve thoracic vertebrae (T1–T12) forming the posterior thoracic wall. Each articulates with a pair of ribs via costovertebral joints. On CT: assess vertebral body height and density (compression fractures, metastases), pedicles, spinal canal diameter, and disc spaces.

name: Left Paraspinal Muscles
description: Twelve thoracic vertebrae (T1–T12) forming the posterior thoracic wall. Each articulates with a pair of ribs via costovertebral joints. On CT: assess vertebral body height and density (compression fractures, metastases), pedicles, spinal canal diameter, and disc spaces.

name: Right Paraspinal Muscles
description: Twelve thoracic vertebrae (T1–T12) forming the posterior thoracic wall. Each articulates with a pair of ribs via costovertebral joints. On CT: assess vertebral body height and density (compression fractures, metastases), pedicles, spinal canal diameter, and disc spaces.

name: Sternum
description: Flat bone forming the anterior midline of the thoracic wall. Three parts: manubrium, body, and xiphoid process. The sternal angle (angle of Louis) at the manubriosternal junction marks the level of T4–T5, the aortic arch, and the carina. On CT: assess for fractures, sternal wires (post-sternotomy), and retrosternal masses.

name: Costal Cartilages
description: Flat bone forming the anterior midline of the thoracic wall. Three parts: manubrium, body, and xiphoid process.
